mattmac.bio:
Mattmac, born Matthew Monias, is an Oji-Cree singer, rapper and producer from Garden Hill First Nation in northern Manitoba. Blind from birth, he grew up surrounded by music, sang in his community gospel choir and taught himself beat-making, piano and guitar. His first major public step came through the N’we Jinan mobile studio program, which visited Garden Hill in 2016 and helped him record "Help You See," a song built from his own experience and community perspective.

His 2020 debut project 20/20 pushed that story into a broader national audience. The single "Paradise" reached No. 1 on the Indigenous Music Countdown, and Mattmac’s combination of melodic hooks, hip-hop production and autobiographical writing brought him media attention across Canada. He later won Rap/Electronic Album of the Year at the 2021 Summer Solstice Indigenous Music Awards and continued expanding his catalogue with collaborations, including work connected to artists such as Nelly Furtado and Drezus.

Mattmac’s significance extends beyond an inspirational narrative. He is part of a generation of Indigenous artists using contemporary pop, rap and production tools without separating those sounds from community, place or identity. His career also broadens assumptions about who gets to be a producer and recording artist, making his presence in Northern Dial’s catalogue important both musically and culturally.
mattmac.directory_summary: Garden Hill First Nation artist Mattmac is an Oji-Cree singer, rapper and producer whose melodic hip-hop grew from gospel singing, self-taught production and the N’we Jinan program. His 2020 debut 20/20 and No. 1 Indigenous Music Countdown single "Paradise" brought him national attention, followed by a Summer Solstice Indigenous Music Award. Blind from birth, Mattmac has built a career that foregrounds both contemporary Indigenous music and independent production craft.

kelsi mayne.bio:
Windsor, Ontario singer-songwriter Kelsi Mayne built her career independently, bringing country songwriting into contact with the R&B, soul and pop sounds that travelled across the Detroit River into her hometown. She first developed as a live performer while studying nursing, singing regularly at a Windsor country bar before moving into festival stages, radio and a self-managed recording career. Her 2020 debut album As I Go established that mix of country structure, forceful vocals and wider pop-soul influence.

Mayne’s catalogue continued to grow through singles including "All or Nothing," "Breaking Bad" and "For The Record." "Breaking Bad" reached the Top 50 at Canadian country radio, while "For The Record" earned placement through SiriusXM’s The Highway and major Canadian country playlists. She has also appeared at major Canadian country festivals including Boots and Hearts, Big Valley Jamboree and the Calgary Stampede, while earning multiple CMAOntario nominations and recognition through the International Songwriting Competition.

Her 2026 sophomore album Out of the Blue pushed the independent career into a new phase after years of writing in Nashville and steadily widening her audience. Mayne matters in the Canadian country landscape because her work is rooted in a border-city musical environment where country, Motown, rock and R&B overlap, giving her a sound that is recognizably country without being stylistically narrow.
kelsi mayne.directory_summary: Windsor singer-songwriter Kelsi Mayne is an independent Canadian country artist whose sound mixes country roots with the Motown, R&B, rock and pop influences of her border-city upbringing. Her debut As I Go was followed by radio and streaming momentum for songs including "Breaking Bad" and "For The Record," major festival appearances and multiple CMAOntario nominations. Her 2026 album Out of the Blue marked the next stage of a self-directed career built through touring, songwriting and persistent audience growth.

wave montega.bio:
Toronto rapper Wave Montega emerged from Malton with a style shaped by the multicultural environment of the city’s west end and by the Jamaican music he heard growing up. A published poet from childhood, he began releasing music in 2018 after time in the United States on a basketball scholarship. His early breakout "Side Bag" helped establish a local audience and led into the 2020 project Still Wavy.

Montega’s 2022 album Catharsis widened the sound beyond straightforward rap, moving among drill, grime, R&B and dancehall while keeping his writing focused on depression, relationships, betrayal and loss. That flexibility reflects both Toronto’s genre-crossing rap culture and Montega’s own Caribbean background. Later releases continued the pattern, including METHADONE and 2026 material that kept his catalogue moving between hard-edged street rap and more introspective songs.

His importance in Northern Dial’s contemporary catalogue comes from that refusal to flatten Toronto rap into one sound. Montega’s work connects Malton, Jamaican-Canadian musical memory, UK drill influence and modern independent rap in a way that feels specific to the city rather than generically international.
wave montega.directory_summary: Malton rapper Wave Montega blends Toronto rap with Jamaican musical roots, UK drill influence and a broader mix of grime, R&B and dancehall. A poet from childhood, he began recording in 2018 and built early momentum with "Side Bag" and the project Still Wavy before expanding his range on 2022’s Catharsis. His catalogue pairs street-level detail with unusually introspective writing about depression, relationships and loss.

tariiiq.bio:
Edmonton MC, DJ and producer TARiiiQ, born Tariq Bakir, built his music around the traditions of conscious hip-hop while keeping the production palette deliberately open. Originally from Palestine and based in Edmonton, he first developed as a DJ before moving deeper into rapping and production, drawing on boom-bap, jazz textures and the foundational language of hip-hop.

Since beginning his recording catalogue in 2019, TARiiiQ has expanded beyond traditionalist rap into trap, downtempo, lo-fi and psychedelic production. His 2024 full-length work and subsequent releases helped push his catalogue past half a million collective streams, while performances with a full band have taken him to venues and festivals including Edmonton’s Starlite Room, North Country Fair, JazzFest, Starbelly Jam and Shambhala.

Activism is central to his writing rather than an occasional theme. TARiiiQ has used hip-hop to address occupation, violence and Palestinian identity while also celebrating culture and community. Within Canadian rap, that gives his work a distinct role: he connects Edmonton’s independent scene to a wider political hip-hop tradition and treats production versatility as a vehicle for message rather than a substitute for it.
tariiiq.directory_summary: Edmonton-based MC, DJ and producer TARiiiQ, born Tariq Bakir, makes conscious hip-hop shaped by boom-bap foundations, jazz textures and an increasingly wide production palette. Originally from Palestine, he has used his music to address occupation, violence and cultural identity while expanding into trap, lo-fi, downtempo and psychedelic sounds. Since 2019, his independent catalogue and full-band performances have connected Edmonton’s rap scene with a broader tradition of politically engaged hip-hop.

playingwithfire.bio:
Hamilton, Ontario alternative-rock band playingwithfire formed in 2020 around vocalist-guitarist Campbell Coleman and drummer Brandon Roussell, later expanding with keyboardist Robert Bisset. With the pandemic limiting conventional rehearsals and live development during the group’s earliest period, much of its initial songwriting took shape remotely before the band moved into regular performance and recording.

The group’s sound draws from several strands of modern rock rather than a single revival lane, combining gritty guitar work with post-punk melody, electronic-rock textures and introspective songwriting. Early songs such as "Shivering" established that approach, while later releases pushed toward a darker and more atmospheric presentation. In 2026 the band issued the five-track project Monologues at Midnight, including "Erased," "Silhouette" and "Fallback."

playingwithfire is still an emerging act, so its significance is less about established awards than about documenting a developing Ontario rock voice while the story is still unfolding. Northern Dial’s profile captures the band at that stage: locally grounded, independently built and still defining how far its hybrid alternative-rock sound can travel.
playingwithfire.directory_summary: Hamilton alternative-rock band playingwithfire formed in 2020 around Campbell Coleman and Brandon Roussell, later adding Robert Bisset. The group blends guitar-driven rock with post-punk melody, electronic textures and introspective writing, moving from early songs such as "Shivering" toward the darker 2026 project Monologues at Midnight. Still early in its career, playingwithfire represents the kind of developing Ontario rock act Northern Dial aims to document before the larger narrative is settled.

grace of arc.bio:
Montréal singer, songwriter, musician and producer Grace of Arc makes alternative rock built around cinematic atmosphere, heavy dynamics and emotionally direct writing. Raised in a music-filled household and writing from a young age, Grace developed a style that pulls from rock, metal, opera, jazz and modern alternative pop rather than treating those influences as separate worlds.

The project began gaining wider attention with "Sides Of Me I’ve Never Met," which was selected as a SOCAN Song of the Week. Grace subsequently earned Spotify editorial support through playlists including ALT_QC and Fresh Finds Heavy, while 2026 singles such as "Rotten" and "La fin" continued sharpening the project’s dark, theatrical sound. Grace has also participated in artist-development programs including Canada’s Music Incubator and SOCAN Kenekt.

As a queer, non-binary artist of colour working in indie and alternative rock, Grace of Arc brings a perspective still underrepresented in those scenes. The project’s importance is not simply representational, though: the music is deliberately ambitious in its arrangement and production, making Grace part of a Montréal alternative ecosystem where genre, language and identity increasingly overlap.
grace of arc.directory_summary: Montréal artist Grace of Arc makes cinematic alternative rock that moves among heavy guitars, dark pop atmosphere and emotionally direct songwriting. "Sides Of Me I’ve Never Met" earned SOCAN recognition, while later singles including "Rotten" and "La fin" received growing editorial support. A queer, non-binary artist of colour, Grace also brings a still-underrepresented perspective to Canadian indie rock while maintaining a strong focus on production, arrangement and theatrical scale.

suckerpunch!.bio:
Montréal pop-punk band SUCKERPUNCH! has built its identity around a deliberately direct, high-energy update of the genre’s early-2000s vocabulary. Rather than treating pop-punk as nostalgia alone, the group pairs big melodic hooks and fast guitar arrangements with modern production and a playful self-description built around keeping the music fun, immediate and communal.

The band’s independent releases developed into a rapidly expanding audience through songs such as "99," "Out of My Mind" and "SURVIVE YOU." In 2025 SUCKERPUNCH! signed with Nettwerk Music Group, giving the Montréal group a larger platform as it moved into its 2026 release cycle. The EP WORST PARTY EVER collected singles including "F.O.M.O.," "STANDING OVATION," "TROUBLE" and "RICH!," with a deluxe edition following in September 2026.

Streaming growth, editorial playlist support and appearances around the renewed pop-punk festival circuit have made SUCKERPUNCH! one of the more visible young Canadian bands working in the style. Their role in Northern Dial is as a snapshot of a genre revival that is no longer simply looking backward: Montréal musicians are using the old pop-punk framework as a contemporary independent scene of their own.
suckerpunch!.directory_summary: Montréal six-piece SUCKERPUNCH! is part of the current Canadian pop-punk revival, pairing early-2000s energy with modern production and a deliberately playful live identity. After building momentum with songs such as "99" and "Out of My Mind," the band signed with Nettwerk in 2025 and released the 2026 EP WORST PARTY EVER. Growing streaming numbers, editorial playlist support and festival appearances have turned the group into a visible new voice in Montréal’s guitar-driven scene.

vibi.bio:
Canadian singer-songwriter VIBI developed a pop sound around a raspy, powerful vocal tone and diaristic songwriting, later relocating to Los Angeles while maintaining her Canadian identity. Her work combines singer-songwriter intimacy with polished Scandinavian-influenced pop production, allowing her to move between stripped emotional writing and larger, hook-driven arrangements.

Mentorship connected to the Stargate production world helped sharpen that pop vocabulary, while the Rain In California project earned placement on Spotify and Amazon Music editorial playlists. VIBI also opened for Bryan Adams before a crowd of roughly 60,000 and won the pop category grand prize in the John Lennon Songwriting Contest, giving her independent career notable performance and songwriting milestones beyond streaming alone.

Her subsequent catalogue has expanded quickly through releases including Mattress, we had fun, didn’t we?, "homesafe," "killshot" and the 2026 EP angeldies. VIBI’s strongest through-line is emotional specificity: even as the production grows more polished, the songs remain centred on vulnerable, conversational writing rather than anonymous pop architecture.
vibi.directory_summary: Canadian singer-songwriter VIBI pairs a distinctive raspy voice with confessional pop writing and polished production. The Rain In California project earned editorial playlist support, while her independent career has included opening for Bryan Adams and winning the pop grand prize in the John Lennon Songwriting Contest. Later releases including Mattress, we had fun, didn’t we?, "killshot" and 2026’s angeldies have continued building an increasingly international audience around emotionally direct songwriting.

a girl named sue.bio:
A Girl Named Sue is the solo project of Montréal-born artist and producer Charlie Kunce-Belhadj. Working independently and handling her own production, she has built a catalogue that moves through atmospheric electronic pop, drum and bass and emotionally understated songwriting rather than staying within a single genre lane.

The project expanded through a run of collaborative and solo releases in 2025 and 2026, including the Moonsoak EP, "April," "Ma Chance" and "All U Need." Collaborations with artists including Tora and IMANU helped place her voice inside a wider electronic network, while "Ma Chance" also reached francophone Canadian radio and chart contexts.

For Northern Dial, A Girl Named Sue is an example of a Montréal artist whose career is developing through self-production and international electronic collaboration rather than a conventional band or singer-songwriter route. The catalogue is still young, but the combination of independent production, bilingual context and fast-moving electronic work makes the project worth documenting early.
a girl named sue.directory_summary: Montréal-born artist and producer Charlie Kunce-Belhadj records as A Girl Named Sue, an independent project moving between electronic pop, drum and bass and intimate songwriting. Releases including the Moonsoak EP, "April" and "Ma Chance" have been joined by collaborations with Tora and IMANU, placing the project inside a wider international electronic network. Her self-produced approach makes A Girl Named Sue a notable emerging Montréal voice to follow as the catalogue develops.

clairmont the second.bio:
Born and raised in Toronto’s Weston neighbourhood, Clairmont The Second, born Clairmont II Humphrey, developed as a true multi-hyphenate: rapper, vocalist, producer, composer, engineer, director, editor, filmmaker and photographer. His early self-released mixtapes led into the 2016 album Quest for Milk and Honey, which was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize and established him as an artist whose production and visual language were inseparable from the writing.

The 2017 album Lil Mont from the Ave earned a JUNO nomination for Rap Recording of the Year, while later work including Do You Drive? and It’s Not How It Sounds continued his self-produced, highly authored approach. His song "Grip" was shortlisted for the SOCAN Songwriting Prize in 2020, followed by another shortlist for "Dream" in 2021. He also received the Prism Prize’s Hi-Fidelity Award for his work in music video, reinforcing how central directing and visual storytelling are to his practice.

Clairmont’s influence is especially important within Toronto’s independent hip-hop ecosystem. He represents a model in which an artist does not simply rap over production but controls the wider sonic and visual world around the music. Collaborations and production relationships across Toronto’s alternative R&B and rap scenes have made him a connective figure between neighbourhood-rooted hip-hop, experimental composition and independent filmmaking.
clairmont the second.directory_summary: Weston-born Clairmont The Second is a Toronto rapper, producer, composer and filmmaker whose independent practice treats music and visual storytelling as one body of work. Quest for Milk and Honey earned Polaris recognition, Lil Mont from the Ave received a JUNO nomination and songs including "Grip" and "Dream" reached the SOCAN Songwriting Prize shortlist. His self-produced catalogue has made him an important link between Toronto hip-hop, alternative R&B and multidisciplinary independent art.
